A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the title change. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original image-generation experiments on four datasets, synthetic coupling comparisons and ablations in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds ECT results in Table 2 and ImageNet sensitivity results in Appendix C.

M1.justification: The GC endpoint construction, consistency loss, frozen-predictor option and probabilistic IC/GC mixture are retained. v3's explicit mixture loss and masking pseudocode document the procedure already described in v2 Section 5.3. ECT reuses this GC mechanism under another training recipe.

E1.justification: Both versions use CIFAR-10, ImageNet-32, CelebA-64, LSUN Church-64 and the two-Dirac synthetic example. The ECT comparison and ImageNet sensitivity study retain existing data and task coverage; pretrained initialization changes experimental settings.

E2.justification: v3 adds ECT-IC as an evaluated comparator to ECT-GC in Table 2 under short and long training budgets. The existing iCT-IC and iCT-OT comparisons remain.

E3.justification: Section 5.3 adds diffusion-initialized ECT fine-tuning with approximately one-GPU-hour and 100k-step budgets, using GC mixing probability 0.3. The listed ImageNet dropout candidate also changes from [0, 0.2, 0.2] in v2 Table 5 to [0, 0, 0.2, 0.2] in v3 Table 6. This establishes a reported setting revision, without establishing reruns.

E4.justification: v3 Appendix C.1 and Figure 9 add an ImageNet-32 sensitivity study over mixing probabilities 0.3, 0.5, 0.7 and 1. Existing CIFAR-10 mixing, distribution-shift, timestep, dropout, EMA and equal-time analyses remain; the GC-only failure analysis moves into the appendix.

E5.justification: Both versions describe five evaluation resamplings from the same trained model for Table 1 uncertainty. The added ECT results use the existing plus/minus reporting style, without introducing a stated new run-count, seed, confidence-interval or significance-testing procedure.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the retained ablation table have identical numerical entries. v3 Table 2 adds ECT-IC/ECT-GC FIDs of 7.37/6.41 for short training and 4.11/3.74 for long training. Figure 9 adds ImageNet learning curves showing advantages for mixing probabilities 0.3 and 0.5.

T1.justification: The theorem, lemma and corollary statements and their proofs are retained. Appendix A.3 adds an explanatory overview of existing transport-equation reasoning, and the Gaussian toy derivation moves there from the main text. The explicit mixture equation formalizes the previously described mixture.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central contributions: the persistent training/distillation discrepancy, GC's reduction of its proxy and transport cost, and improved training convergence and performance. The revised terminology and abstract emphasis on proofs do not introduce a new core contribution.

C2.justification: v3 elaborates the noise-dependence interpretation of transport cost and connects joint training more explicitly to the ideal-predictor assumption. Appendix D adds regime-dependent mixing recommendations, including caution about large values in ECT. Conversely, it removes v2's explicit qualification that smaller models and batches explain weaker iCT baseline performance.

D1.justification: v3 supplies explicit model scaling functions, the weak endpoint predictor's 20k-step pretraining budget, per-example mixing-mask pseudocode and mixing-parameter selection guidance. Most architecture, preprocessing, hardware and code-access information is retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Geng et al.'s ECT work and discusses concurrent continuous-time consistency models by Lu and Song. The broader positioning against independent coupling, minibatch OT and flow methods remains. Li et al.'s publication update concerns an already cited work.

P1.justification: Sections 4–5 substantially reframe the narrative around an ideal predictor, frozen pretraining and joint learning. Terminology changes throughout from generator-induced to generator-augmented and from mixing to joint learning. The GC-only diagnostic section and Gaussian example move to appendices, whose organization also changes.

P2.justification: v3 adopts a two-column main text and references, with extensively resized and repositioned displays. The transport-cost figure is split between a CIFAR-only main figure and the retained two-panel appendix figure; the algorithm and GC-only plots move to appendices. ECT Table 2 and ImageNet Figure 9 are added.

improvement.justification: The ECT comparison and ImageNet sensitivity study modestly strengthen empirical support, while explicit mixture pseudocode and predictor explanations improve reproducibility and clarity. These gains outweigh the lost caveat about smaller iCT models and batches and the unexplained ImageNet dropout revision. The central benchmark results and proofs remain unchanged.
